title_en: Where Was It Ever Heard or Seen
en_note: Machine translation by Claude (my reading), not on Pesna.org and not checked by a native speaker. Treat it as a study aid.
translator_notes: 'к'носани' is my reading of 'кина-носани' (hennaed nails), and 'набелено' as whitened/made up with cosmetics; both are guesses. 'јамди аман' is a refrain exclamation, rendered as left-in-transliteration.

lines.en: Where was it ever heard or seen,
that a bishop should turn Turk,

lines.cyr: владика турчин да стани, јамди аман,
lines.lat: vladika turčin da stani, jamdi aman,
lines.en: that a bishop should turn Turk, yamdi aman,
for one whitened (painted) face.
For one whitened face
and for a set of hennaed nails,

lines.cyr: за едно лице набелено, јамди аман,
lines.lat: za edno lice nabeleno, jamdi aman,
lines.en: for one whitened face, yamdi aman,
and for a set of hennaed nails.
Everyone goes to the market,
the bishop goes to the barber,

lines.cyr: владика оди на бербер, јамди аман,
lines.lat: vladika odi na berber, jamdi aman,
lines.en: the bishop goes to the barber, yamdi aman,
to have his beard shaved off.
When they were shaving his beard,
ninety eyes were watching,
ninety eyes were watching, yamdi aman,
a hundred and fifty candles were shining.
Everyone goes to church,
the bishop goes to the mosque,

lines.cyr: владика оди в џамија, јамди аман,
lines.lat: vladika odi v džamija, jamdi aman,
lines.en: the bishop goes to the mosque, yamdi aman,
to change his faith.
When they were changing his faith,
a hundred and fifty hodjas were singing,

lines.cyr: сто и педесет оџи пееа, јамди аман,
lines.lat: sto i pedeset odži peea, jamdi aman,
lines.en: a hundred and fifty hodjas were singing, yamdi aman,
ninety candles were burning.
They gave him a fine name,
Asan the brave, turned Turk,
Asan the brave, turned Turk, yamdi aman,
who is changing his faith.
